fullPassage:
My Octopus Teacher

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.

First Encounter

I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's perspective, I left a camera near the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped the environment around the den. Expecting some drama to come, I waited.

Making Friends

The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way to the top. There I was, just staring into the eyes of this incredible creature. It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I learned was that "it" was a "she."

Getting Closer

Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster.

The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

The next day, I was relieved to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to witness these things happening to her.

Recovery, Growth, and Sacrifice

A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too.

An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.

After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.

I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.

questions.passage: I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the (A)[dense / sparse] seaweed forests where I met an octopus. I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a (B)[heap / lack] of shells. Suddenly, an octopus (C)[sprang / retreated] from the heap and grabbed the fish.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 빽빽한(dense) 해조류 숲에서 문어를 만났고, 조개 더미(heap) 근처에서 문어가 튀어나왔다(sprang).
det.analysis:
✅ ① dense — heap — sprang: 원문 그대로
❌ ② sparse(드문): dense(빽빽한)의 반의어
❌ ③ lack(부족): heap(더미)의 반의어 맥락
❌ ④ retreated(후퇴했다): sprang(튀어나왔다)의 반의어
det.tip: dense(빽빽한) ↔ sparse(드문), heap(더미) ↔ lack(부족), sprang(튀어나오다) ↔ retreated(후퇴하다)

questions.passage: To see the world from the octopus's (A)[perspective / ignorance], I left a camera near the den and started visiting (B)[regularly / rarely]. I even (C)[mapped / ignored] the environment around the den.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 문어의 관점(perspective)에서 세계를 보기 위해 정기적으로(regularly) 방문하기 시작했고, 굴 주변 환경을 지도로 그렸다(mapped).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ perspective — regularly — mapped: 원문 일치
❌ ① ignorance(무지): perspective(관점)과 반대 맥락
❌ ② rarely(드물게): regularly(정기적으로)의 반의어
❌ ④ ignored(무시했다): mapped(지도로 만들었다)의 반의어 맥락
det.tip: perspective(관점) ↔ ignorance(무지), regularly(정기적으로) ↔ rarely(드물게), mapped(지도화하다) ↔ ignored(무시하다)

questions.passage: It was (A)[bittersweet / delightful] knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young. After mating, she didn't come out of her den. She was timing her final moments for the (B)[hatching / abandoning] of her eggs. As a human being, I found something (C)[noble / trivial] in that sacrifice.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 마지막 날이 다가오고 있다는 것을 아는 것은 씁쓸한(bittersweet) 일이었고, 알의 부화(hatching)를 위해 마지막 순간을 맞추고 있었으며, 그 희생에서 고귀한(noble) 것을 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② bittersweet — hatching — noble: 원문 일치
❌ ① delightful(즐거운): 죽음을 앞둔 상황에서 단순히 즐겁다는 부적절
❌ ③ abandoning(버리기): hatching(부화)의 반대 맥락
❌ ④ trivial(사소한): noble(고귀한)의 반의어
det.tip: bittersweet = 씁쓸달콤한 (기쁨과 슬픔이 공존). hatching = 부화. noble(고귀한) ↔ trivial(사소한)

questions.passage: Amazed at the ①<u>cleverness</u> of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an ②<u>ordinary</u> creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's ③<u>perspective</u>, I left a camera near the ④<u>den</u> and started visiting regularly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정말 비범한(extraordinary) 생물이구나! ordinary(평범한)는 extraordinary(비범한)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② ordinary(평범한) → extraordinary(비범한)가 원문. 해조류로 위장하는 놀라운 행동 후 감탄하는 문맥에 ordinary는 부적절
❌ ① cleverness(영리함): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ perspective(관점): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ den(굴): 원문 그대로
det.tip: extraordinary(비범한) = extra-(넘어서는) + ordinary(평범한). 감탄문 What an ~! 뒤에는 긍정적/강렬한 표현

questions.passage: Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest ①<u>predators</u>, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark ②<u>tracking</u> her. In an ③<u>instant</u>, she swam into a crack to ④<u>approach</u>, but the shark was faster.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 순간적으로 그녀는 틈으로 헤엄쳐 도망갔다(escape). approach(접근하다)는 escape(도망치다)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ approach(접근하다) → escape(도망치다)가 원문. 상어를 피해 도망가는 문맥에 approach는 부적절
❌ ① predators(포식자): 원문 그대로
❌ ② tracking(추적하는): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ instant(순간): 원문 그대로
det.tip: escape(도망치다) ↔ approach(접근하다). 상어가 추적하고 있으므로 문어는 도망가야 함

questions.passage: I started to compare my life to life in the ①<u>unforgiving</u> sea. I thought of what was ②<u>valuable</u> in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends. An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after ③<u>reproducing</u>. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young. Eventually, she ④<u>abandoned</u> herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 결국 그녀는 죽기 전에 새끼의 탄생을 보호하는 데 자신을 바쳤다(committed). abandoned(버렸다)는 committed(헌신했다)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ abandoned(버렸다) → committed(헌신했다)가 원문. 새끼를 위해 헌신하는 문맥에 abandoned는 부적절
❌ ① unforgiving(가혹한): 원문 그대로
❌ ② valuable(가치 있는): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ reproducing(번식): 원문 그대로
det.tip: committed herself to(~에 헌신했다) ↔ abandoned(버렸다). commit oneself to = ~에 전념하다

questions.passage: She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans. The next day, I was __________ to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다음 날, 그녀가 생존한 것을 보고 안도했다(relieved).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ relieved(안도한): 생존 소식에 대한 긍정적 감정. 원문 일치
❌ ① horrified(충격받은): 생존은 좋은 소식이므로 부적합
❌ ② disappointed(실망한): 생존에 대해 실망할 이유 없음
❌ ④ confused(혼란스러운): 문맥과 맞지 않음
det.tip: relieved = 안도한. 위험한 상황 후 무사한 것을 확인할 때 사용

questions.passage: There I was, just staring into the eyes of this __________ creature. It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 놀라운(incredible) 생물의 눈을 바라보고 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ incredible(놀라운): 호기심을 자극하고 marvelous와 같은 맥락의 긍정적 감탄. 원문 일치
❌ ① ordinary(평범한): 호기심과 감탄의 문맥에 어울리지 않음
❌ ② frightening(무서운): 신뢰를 얻는 우호적 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ artificial(인공적인): 야생 문어에 대한 설명으로 부적합
det.tip: incredible = 놀라운, 믿기 어려운. sparked my curiosity가 단서 → 호기심을 자극할 만큼 놀라운 존재

questions.passage: I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 인간으로서 나는 그 희생(sacrifice)에서 고귀한 것을 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② sacrifice(희생): 새끼를 위해 목숨을 바친 행위. 원문 일치
❌ ① curiosity(호기심): 고귀함과 연결되는 문맥이 아님
❌ ③ competition(경쟁): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ escape(도망): 헌신/희생과 반대 개념
det.tip: sacrifice = 희생. commit oneself to protecting → noble sacrifice. 자신의 목숨을 바쳐 새끼를 보호

questions.passage: I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the <u>dense</u> seaweed forests where I met an octopus.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dense와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 빽빽한(dense) 해조류 숲 속에서 문어를 만났다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② thick(빽빽한): dense의 동의어
❌ ① thin(얇은): dense의 반의어
❌ ③ shallow(얕은): 깊이 관련어, dense와 무관
❌ ④ narrow(좁은): 폭 관련어, dense와 무관
det.tip: dense = thick = 빽빽한, 밀집한. dense forest = thick forest

questions.passage: It <u>sparked</u> my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 sparked와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이전에 경험하지 못했던 방식으로 호기심을 촉발시켰다(sparked).
det.analysis:
✅ ① triggered(촉발시킨): sparked의 동의어. 자극/시작의 의미
❌ ② diminished(줄어든): 호기심이 줄어든 것이 아닌 촉발
❌ ③ concealed(숨긴): sparked와 반대 맥락
❌ ④ delayed(지연시킨): 호기심을 지연시키는 것은 문맥에 맞지 않음
det.tip: spark = trigger = ignite (촉발하다, 불 붙이다). spark one's curiosity = 호기심을 자극하다

questions.passage: I wanted to learn more about this <u>marvelous</u> creature. The first thing I learned was that "it" was a "she."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 marvelous와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이 경이로운(marvelous) 생물에 대해 더 배우고 싶었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ wonderful(훌륭한): marvelous의 동의어
❌ ① dangerous(위험한): 감탄의 맥락이 아님
❌ ② ordinary(평범한): marvelous의 반의어
❌ ④ mysterious(신비로운): 유사하지만 marvelous는 경탄의 뉘앙스
det.tip: marvelous = wonderful = amazing = incredible (경이로운, 놀라운). marvel(경이) → marvelous

questions.passage: She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was <u>bleeding</u>. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the <u>opportunity</u> to get back to her den. The next day, I was relieved to see that she had <u>survived</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 survived와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 그녀가 생존한(survived) 것을 보고 안도했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ perished(죽었다): survived의 반의어
❌ ① endured(견뎠다): survived와 유사한 의미
❌ ② lived(살았다): survived의 동의어
❌ ③ recovered(회복했다): survived와 유사한 맥락
det.tip: survived(생존했다) ↔ perished(죽었다). perish = die = 죽다, 소멸하다

questions.passage: I started to compare my life to life in the <u>unforgiving</u> sea. I thought of what was valuable in life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 unforgiving과 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 가혹한(unforgiving) 바다에서의 삶과 내 삶을 비교하기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① merciful(자비로운): unforgiving의 반의어
❌ ② harsh(가혹한): unforgiving의 동의어
❌ ③ cruel(잔인한): unforgiving의 동의어
❌ ④ ruthless(무자비한): unforgiving의 동의어
det.tip: unforgiving(가혹한, 용서 없는) ↔ merciful(자비로운). un- + forgiving = 용서하지 않는

questions.passage:
(A) She was in serious danger because her arms <u>function</u> like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

(B) The main <u>function</u> of the event was to raise funds for charity.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 function의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 팔이 인간의 손, 다리, 코, 눈처럼 기능한다(function). (B) 그 행사(function)의 주요 목적은 자선 기금 모금이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 기능하다 — 행사: (A) 동사 function = 기능하다, (B) 명사 function = 행사/기능
❌ ① 행사 — 기능하다: (A)와 (B) 의미 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 기능하다 — 기능하다: (B)에서 function은 명사 '행사'
❌ ④ 행사 — 행사: (A)에서 function은 동사 '기능하다'
det.tip: function 다의어: ① (동사) 기능하다, 작동하다 ② (명사) 기능, 역할 ③ (명사) 행사, 공식 모임

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"an animal that naturally preys on others"

det.korean: 다른 동물을 자연적으로 잡아먹는 동물 = 포식자(predator)
det.analysis:
✅ ① predator(포식자): 영영 정의에 정확히 부합
❌ ② prey(먹이): 잡아먹히는 대상
❌ ③ companion(동반자): 포식과 무관
❌ ④ observer(관찰자): 포식과 무관
det.tip: predator(포식자) ↔ prey(먹이). predator = an animal that hunts and kills other animals

questions.passage: A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my __________ (amaze), a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 나의 놀라움(amazement)에, 작은 팔이 다시 자라기 시작했다.
det.analysis: amaze(동사: 놀라게 하다) → amazement(명사: 놀라움). to my 뒤에 명사 필요.
det.tip: amaze(v.) → amazement(n.). to my amazement = 놀랍게도. 전치사 to + 소유격 my + 명사

questions.passage: I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more __________ (function), I felt things in my life were improving too.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 문어의 팔이 더 기능적이(functional) 되자, 내 삶도 나아지고 있다고 느꼈다.
det.analysis: function(명사/동사) → functional(형용사). more 뒤에 형용사 필요 (비교급).
det.tip: function(n./v.) → functional(adj.). more functional = 더 기능적인. -al 접미사 → 형용사화

questions.passage: The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to __________, I swam toward the surface.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 숨을 쉬어야 했기(take a breath) 때문에 수면을 향해 헤엄쳤다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② take a breath(숨을 쉬다): 다이빙 후 수면으로 올라가는 이유. 원문 일치
❌ ① find food(먹이 찾기): 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ avoid sharks(상어 피하기): 이 장면에서 상어 언급 없음
❌ ④ check the camera(카메라 확인): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: take a breath = 숨을 쉬다. 다이빙 중이므로 수면으로 올라가 숨을 쉬어야 함

questions.passage: She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was __________ just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a dangerous predator in the sea
a temporary visitor to the ocean

det.korean: 그녀는 단순한 문어가 아니라 내가 지금 그러하듯이 이 세계의 일부(a part of this world)였다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ a part of this world: 'just as I am a part of it now'에서 it = this world. 대칭 구조
❌ ① dangerous predator: 문어는 포식자가 아님 (상어가 포식자)
❌ ② ordinary creature without emotions: smart, sensitive, strong과 모순
❌ ④ temporary visitor: 원문의 영속적 연결과 맞지 않음
det.tip: just as I am a part of it = 내가 그 일부인 것처럼. it = this world. 대칭 구조를 통해 빈칸 추론
